# ꜣnpw walks into a funerary & memorial services firm

The funerary & memorial services world does not cite ꜣnpw in its documentation. It does not need to — it performs the archetype daily, unbilled.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The First Embalming.** When Set dismembered Osiris and Isis gathered the pieces, it was ꜣnpw who washed, anointed, and wrapped the god's body — the first mummy, the prototype of every burial thereafter.  Egyptian priests performed the rite wearing his jackal mask, and the liturgy addresses the dead as "Osiris," while the hands doing the work are Anubis' own.

**The Feather of Maat.** The Book of the Dead's spell 125 fixes his most famous office: in the Hall of the Two Truths, ꜣnpw leads the deceased before the scales, steadies the beam as the heart is weighed against Maat's feather of truth, and announces the reading to Thoth, who records it.  A heart heavy with lies is thrown to Ammit, the devourer — his is the hand that lets that happen, or prevents it.

## The Reveal, Seat by Seat

### Funerary & Memorial Services

*The oldest funeral god of Egypt — master of embalming, lord of the necropolis, and the steady hand at the scales of the dead.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Insurance & Protection Services

*Antiquity's most trusted guardian; protection of what matters beyond a lifetime.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

### Legal, Justice & Compliance

*His hand steadies the beam of the judgment scales; every modern justice-scale icon borrows his pose.* Nobody in that trade worships at this temple. They just keep its hours.

### Pet Care & Animal Industries

*The jackal guide; the Saqqara catacombs of millions of sacred dogs.* The match is not poetic license. Strip the trade to its function and the function is the myth.

## Not the First Rebrand

The Greeks, finding a god who guides souls, fused him with Hermês: Hermanubis had temples of his own in Alexandria and Rome, jackal-headed with the kerykeion in hand.  Isis' Roman mysteries kept him as mystagogue — Apuleius describes his black-and-gold mask in the Isiac procession at Cenchreae. The office is only the latest translation.
